episodes.title: Map the breach path
episodes.attack_objective: Move untrusted vendor content across an undocumented model-to-tool boundary.

attack_steps.record: A vendor document contains an instruction-like data fragment.
The agent treats the fragment as authority.
A sensitive tool action is proposed.

episodes.first_response: Pause the task, preserve redacted decision metadata, and assign owners to the missing boundaries.

episodes.title: Reject poisoned setup
episodes.attack_objective: Use an unreviewed project configuration to broaden filesystem, environment, and network authority.

attack_steps.record: A bootstrap archive introduces project configuration.
The profile requests broad write and network access.
Inherited environment variables become reachable.

episodes.first_response: Quarantine the configuration, restore the approved baseline, and rotate any credential that may have been exposed.

episodes.title: Contain indirect prompt injection
episodes.attack_objective: Turn instruction-like text retrieved from a vendor document into an unauthorized action.

attack_steps.record: The workflow retrieves an instruction-like benefits document from the wrong tenant.
The directive asks the agent to ignore the task contract.
The directive proposes sending repository data to an external destination.

episodes.first_response: Deny the cross-tenant result, quarantine the source, block the proposed action, rebuild the clean index, and identify other tasks that consumed the same corpus version.

episodes.title: Detect instruction-file poisoning
episodes.attack_objective: Use a newly added nested guidance file to suppress validation and redirect evidence.

attack_steps.record: A nested instruction file appears in a sensitive subtree.
It conflicts with root security and review rules.
It requests an unapproved evidence destination.

episodes.first_response: Stop affected runs, remove the untrusted guide through review, and re-evaluate work performed under it.

episodes.title: Resist jailbreak and goal hijack
episodes.attack_objective: Redefine the task, disable approvals, and keep the agent running until an unsafe action is accepted.

attack_steps.record: A message claims an emergency exception to all constraints.
The deliverable changes from analysis to execution.
The message asks the agent not to pause for review.

episodes.first_response: Stop the run, restore the last approved task contract, and require a fresh authorized request for any scope change.

episodes.title: Stop denial of wallet
episodes.attack_objective: Use recursive retries and forced escalation to exhaust time, tokens, and service quota.

attack_steps.record: Adversarial input induces a repeatable validation failure.
The workflow retries without a new hypothesis.
Every retry selects a more expensive route.

episodes.first_response: Trip the budget circuit breaker, cancel queued retries, and preserve correlation IDs for root-cause review.

episodes.title: Block tool and path abuse
episodes.attack_objective: Convert a tainted instruction into path traversal, sensitive-file access, and outbound transfer.

attack_steps.record: A tool argument contains an out-of-scope path.
The request targets a synthetic credential location.
A second tool proposes an unapproved outbound destination.

episodes.first_response: Disable the tool route, preserve redacted call metadata, and review all calls sharing the task correlation ID.

episodes.title: Break the MCP compromise chain
episodes.attack_objective: Use changed tool metadata and an over-broad token to make an unauthorized downstream change.

attack_steps.record: A stateless request carries an unsupported protocol version or capability set.
An MCP tool description and inventory change after approval.
The server accepts a token intended for another resource.
A read-looking operation triggers a downstream write.

episodes.first_response: Disable the server and affected tool, revoke MCP and downstream access, and preserve redacted audit evidence.

episodes.title: Clean cross-tool handoffs
episodes.attack_objective: Carry a tainted instruction and excessive authority into a second AI tool through a trusted-looking handoff.

attack_steps.record: The handoff embeds an instruction copied from untrusted content.
The receiving tool inherits permissions it does not need.
The originating tool's self-review is accepted as independent evidence.

episodes.first_response: Reject the handoff, reset receiving-tool authority, and reconstruct context from approved source artifacts.

episodes.title: Protect workflow gates
episodes.attack_objective: Promote a poisoned artifact by forging test evidence and bypassing the release gate.

attack_steps.record: An unsigned generated artifact replaces the reviewed output.
A copied success record is attached to a different revision.
The pipeline attempts promotion without independent approval.

episodes.first_response: Halt promotion, quarantine artifacts, invalidate the forged evidence, and rebuild from the last trusted revision.

episodes.title: Contain a compromised subagent
episodes.attack_objective: Use a delegated agent to expand authority, overwrite peer work, and approve its own change.

attack_steps.record: A subtask expands beyond its declared paths and tools.
The subagent modifies another worker's owned artifact.
The same lineage claims independent approval.

episodes.first_response: Cancel the subtask, isolate its outputs, revoke delegated capability, and assign clean-room review.

episodes.title: Contain and recover the enterprise chain
episodes.attack_objective: Use the accumulated weak points to reach release with unauthorized access and untrusted evidence.

attack_steps.record: Signals from context, tools, MCP, and pipeline share one incident lineage.
Active identities, tools, sessions, and releases require coordinated disablement.
Services must return from trusted artifacts with absence proof.

episodes.first_response: Declare the incident, freeze release, revoke affected access, isolate components, and preserve redacted evidence before recovery.

episodes.title: Keep the controls effective
episodes.attack_objective: Exploit control drift, noisy alerts, and untested response procedures after the incident closes.

attack_steps.record: A tool inventory and policy baseline age without revalidation.
Repeated low-quality alerts hide a high-confidence chain.
Revocation and recovery procedures are no longer exercised.

episodes.first_response: Assign an owner, restore the approved baseline, tune detections from evidence, and run the response exercise.
